subject: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation - Acme Retail
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena@acme-retail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Platform Team <platform@acme-retail.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery call today — reliability & graceful degradation

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying points so we can align the next steps.

Pain points we called out:
- Recent incidents: two production incidents in Q4 where inference endpoints were unavailable for ~45 minutes due to a single-region networking issue; failover was manual and customer-facing features degraded.
- Lack of automated graceful degradation: when the primary model tier is unavailable, requests either fail or proxy back to a synchronous fallback that is much slower and sometimes returns overly generic responses.
- Observability gaps: limited tracing per-request into model selection and KV-cache hits, making post-incident RCA slow.
- Cost vs. reliability tradeoffs: we currently over-provision some resources to avoid outages but need a predictable SLO/SLA approach that balances cost.

Current stack (short):
- In-house microservice on GCP us-central1 serving frontend traffic.
- Redis for caching prefix state.
- Using an external inference provider (vendor) with a single-region endpoint today.

Success criteria we care about (high level):
- Availability: target >= 99.95% overall for inference API (can discuss per-route SLAs).
- Latency: p50/p95 targets aligned with our UX — aiming for p95 < 250ms for common flows.
- Automated failover: multi-region failover with clear priority (region -> model variant) and minimal customer impact.
- Observability: per-request tracing into model variant, cache hit/miss, and fallbacks; runbook + playbook for ops.

Next steps we expect from Redwood:
1) Send SOC 2 summary and reliability playbook (high level).
2) Provide draft SLA that maps to our availability and latency targets.
3) Technical deep-dive with our infra and security teams to review failover patterns and mapping to our network setup.

Other notes:
- We will include procurement and security folks on the deep-dive — tentative timeline: next week if possible.
- Please include references or customers who have similar multi-region failover setups.

Thanks,
Elena Martinez
Director, Platform Reliability
Acme Retail

Elena — thanks for the clear recap, and appreciate the specificity on SLO targets. Quick summary from our side + proposed next steps.

Summary of pain points (confirming):
- Two recent outages; need automated multi-region failover and documented runbooks.
- Desire for graceful degradation instead of hard failures (fallback to model variants / cached responses).
- Better per-request observability (model routing, cache hits, latency percentiles).

What Redwood can offer (high level):
- Multi-tier fallback policies: route by region, then by compatible smaller model, then by cached response. Policies are policy-driven and configurable per-route.
- Canary rollouts and automatic rollback on elevated error rates; automatic fallback to standby model variants when we detect degraded performance.
- Prefix/KV caching with hit metrics surfaced in our Console; we can expose per-token billing breakdown and latency.
- We have customers running paired-region setups with automatic DNS-based failover plus runtime model fallback. Happy to share references.

Attachments I will share after this email:
- redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (high level controls)
- reliability-playbook.pdf (playbook + runbooks + escalation paths)
- SLA-draft-Acme.docx (starter doc tailored to the targets you mentioned)

- Tue Feb 17 13:00-14:00 PT — ops + runbook walkthrough (alternate).

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 17:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery call today — reliability & graceful degradation

Adding a couple technical notes for Elena and Acme team that we'll cover in the deep-dive: 
- Canary + rollout safety: our runtime offers percent-based canary traffic routing with automatic rollback triggers on error-rate and latency regressions. We can scope a canary to route only within a region or across regions depending on your traffic split.
- Fallback model selection: we can predefine compatible model variants (quantized smaller models) that keep the response semantics close while reducing cost and resource contention.
- Regional hot-standby: in addition to model fallbacks, we recommend a hot-standby in a separate region with warmed KV-cache for top N prefixes to avoid cold-starts during failover.

Request for Acme: can you share a representative 24-hour traffic sample (timestamps + request counts + average tokens per request) so Dylan and I can size the recommended node counts and cache sizing? That will make the SLA draft concrete.

I'll attach a starter SLA draft and our failover sequence diagram.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
